newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Trans Power denies planning $1.5 bln issue.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Trans Power denies planning $1.5 bln issue.

text.p: New Zealand's state-owned national grid operator Trans Power on Friday rejected a newspaper report saying it intended to raise NZ$1.5 billion through an international bond issue.
Trans Power said it needed to raise $70 million as part of a repayment of funding in December, but saw no problem raising this amount.

"Contrary to a report in today's National Business Review, Trans Power is not seeking to raise NZ$1.5 billion through an international bond issue," said Trans Power Chief Finance Officer Peter Robertson.
The report said Trans Power plans would be jeopardised if generators Electricity Corporation and Contact Energy carried out threats not to pay new national grid charges.
"The story has bemused the money market because those in the market already know Trans Power has in place a facility which enables it to issue up to NZ$1.5 billion in bonds," Robertson said.
To keep the facility current, he said Trans Power was required under the Securities Act to reissue a prospectus every six months.
"The reissuing of the prospectus enables us to draw on that facility if we need to. It is part of a package of facilities we have in place that enable us to borrow money when we need to."
He said the reissuing did not mean Trans Power was attempting to raise $1.5 billion in international bonds.
"It happens that over the short-term, Trans Power needs to make a $200 million interim repayment of funding in December 1996 of which $130 million has already been raised.

"As the prospectus remains current, we could draw on our domestic facility or any of Trans Power's other funding facilities for the balance of NZ$70 million. Trans Power sees no problem in raising that amount."

Robertson said Trans Power was in negotiation with both state-owned generators over the possible withholding of some $30 million of payments in dispute. He said he did not wish to pre-judge the outcome. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
